task.description:
Implement REQ-170 strictly per the APPROVED design at lib/letflow/design/req170-wasm-wallclock-timeout.md (passed CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR clean, no rework, after a very thorough independent verification given the severity of this design's central finding). Read the full design doc before writing any code -- it documents a genuine, serious divergence (decision 0014's timeout-containment claim is false; the real guarantee this requirement delivers is bounding the CALLER's wait, not terminating guest execution) and you must implement per that honest framing, not paper over it. Use export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" and WASMEX_BUILD=true for wasmex-touching mix commands.

Steps: (1) Create lib/letflow/engine/wasm/call_timeout.ex implementing Letflow.Engine.Wasm.CallTimeout per design section 4.2 exactly: config() type (timeout_ms required); classification() type (:wall_clock_timeout | :not_timeout); classify/1 (pure function over an already-completed Letflow.Engine.PluginInterface.outcome(), substring-matching against the TWO exact literal shapes plugin_interface.ex's handle_yield_result/4 already produces -- read that function's real source yourself before writing classify/1, do not trust the design doc's quoted strings without re-verifying them against the current file, since plugin_interface.ex is unmodified but you must confirm the quotes are still accurate). (2) Extend lib/letflow/engine/wasm/plugin_handler.ex per design section 4.3 EXACTLY and ONLY: handle_node/1 reads one additional node_config key ('timeout_ms', default @default_wasmex_timeout_ms = 5_000); run_guest/2 becomes run_guest/3 with a new timeout_ms parameter; call_export/2 becomes call_export/3, passing timeout_ms as Wasmex.call_function/4's explicit 4th argument. No other change to plugin_handler.ex -- read_fixture/1, start_instance/1, and handle_node/1's outer shape/error handling stay exactly as REQ-165 shipped them. (3) Do NOT modify lib/letflow/engine/plugin_interface.ex AT ALL -- design section 3 established its existing algorithm already delivers AC3 with zero changes; confirm this stays true after your changes by re-running the exact live probes described in design section 1.6 yourself before finishing. (4) Create priv/wasm_fixtures/req170_hang.wat per design section 5.1 (identical shape to req165_hang.wat/req169_hang.wat). (5) Write the moduledoc content per design section 6 EXACTLY, including the full DIVERGENCE statement -- do not soften or omit any clause. (6) Do NOT modify module_registry.ex, capability_gate.ex, or memory_guard.ex.

SAFETY NOTE for your own test-writing: do NOT write any test that reproduces design section 1.5's 32-concurrent-hang saturation scenario inside the normal test suite -- the design explicitly states this would durably occupy wasmex's shared native thread pool for the remainder of any test run it's part of. That finding is recorded as a one-time, this-design-session result only (design section 5.7), not an automated regression test.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: a test through the real, unmodified PluginInterface.invoke/2,3 -> PluginHandler.handle_node/1 entry point asserts a guest blocked in a host call is bounded by the configured timeout_ms and the caller receives a structured {:error, reason} within it (not the outer 30s default) -- with an honesty-clause comment per design section 5.2 item 3 citing that execution itself is not terminated, only the caller's wait is bounded.

AC2: a test verifies wasmex's own documented interrupt-and-keep-Store claim by running it directly against Wasmex.call_function/4 (not through PluginHandler) and asserts the REAL behavior (a crash/exit, not a clean {:error,_}; a second call on the same pid also never replies) -- per design section 5.3, written honestly against what actually happens.

AC3: a test asserts the outer PluginInterface.invoke/3 supervised-task boundary terminates the invocation independently of a longer/no inner wasmex timeout -- per design section 5.4, using invoke_opts timeout_ms shorter than node_config's timeout_ms, asserting the task pid becomes not-alive shortly after invoke/3 returns.

AC4: a test drives two different timeout_ms values through the real entry point and asserts the shorter one binds sooner (loose tolerance, real wall-clock timing, not exact values) -- per design section 5.5.

AC5: a test asserts CallTimeout.classify/1 distinguishes a wall-clock-timeout outcome from ResourceLimits.classify_call_result/1's fuel-exhaustion/trap outcomes, both by type-shape and by disjoint substring, per design section 5.6.

AC6: a moduledoc-content test confirms the OQ-5 discipline statement (not settled here; names what would settle it) and the node-wide worker-pool-exhaustion finding are both present, per design section 5.7.
AC7: mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass, real output quoted.
Run mix format on every file you write/edit before finishing.

result.status: COMPLETED -- implemented per the approved design with no deviations found necessary
result.summary: Implemented Letflow.Engine.Wasm.CallTimeout (lib/letflow/engine/wasm/call_timeout.ex) per design section 4.2 exactly -- config()/classification() types, classify/1 substring-matching against the two literal shapes handle_yield_result/4 (plugin_interface.ex lines 217-224) actually produces. I re-read plugin_interface.ex's current source directly before writing classify/1 and confirmed both quoted strings ('plugin handler ' <> inspect(handler) <> ' crashed: ' <> format_exit_reason(reason), and '... did not respond within ...ms') are byte-for-byte unchanged from the design doc's quotes -- no drift. Extended plugin_handler.ex per section 4.3 ONLY: added @default_wasmex_timeout_ms 5_000, handle_node/1 now reads node_config['timeout_ms'], run_guest/2 -> run_guest/3, call_export/2 -> call_export/3 passing timeout_ms as Wasmex.call_function/4's explicit 4th arg. read_fixture/1, start_instance/1, and handle_node/1's outer shape/error handling are byte-identical to before. plugin_interface.ex was NOT touched at all (confirmed via `git diff --stat` against main: empty, and the pre-existing plugin_handler_test.exs 'AC6: plugin_interface.ex is unmodified' test still passes). Re-ran design section 1.6's live probe myself as the new AC3 test (Task.Supervisor.async_nolink + Task.yield(500) + Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill) against a hang guest configured with a 60_000ms inner timeout_ms) -- confirmed live: Task.yield returns nil at ~500ms, the task pid is Process.alive?/1 == false shortly after shutdown, independent of the much longer inner bound. plugin_interface.ex's existing algorithm still delivers AC3 with zero changes, exactly as design section 3 claims. priv/wasm_fixtures/req170_hang.wat already existed on this branch (committed during the design/CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR phase, commit 27c97c7) -- identical shape to req165_hang.wat/req169_hang.wat, verified content matches design section 5.1, no changes needed. Moduledoc written per design section 6 verbatim in substance, including the full DIVERGENCE statement, the 'what DOES hold' / 'what this module does NOT claim' clauses, and an additional 'Node-wide worker-pool-exhaustion finding' section carrying section 8's OQ-5 filing content (candidate scope for a future cap on concurrently in-flight WASM invocations) so AC6's moduledoc-content test has real prose to assert against. Tests written: test/letflow/engine/wasm/call_timeout_test.exs (AC2 direct-against-Wasmex.call_function/4 test asserting the real crash/exit and permanently-wedged-Store shapes via `catch :exit, reason`; AC5 tests pairing a real captured wall-clock-timeout PluginInterface outcome against a real captured ResourceLimits fuel-exhaustion classification, asserting both type-shape and disjoint-substring properties in both directions, plus pure classify/1 unit coverage; AC6 moduledoc-content tests for the OQ-5 discipline statement and the worker-pool-exhaustion filing) and additions to test/letflow/engine/wasm/plugin_handler_test.exs (AC1 test through the real PluginInterface.invoke/2 -> PluginHandler.handle_node/1 entry point, with the required honesty-clause assertion-message comment; AC3 test per above; AC4 test driving timeout_ms 300 vs 2_000 and asserting the shorter elapses faster, loose real-wall-clock tolerance, no exact-ms assertions). test/specs/REQ-170.md rewritten as a short AC-to-test traceability table per this project's established convention. Explicitly did NOT reproduce design section 1.5's 32-concurrent-hang worker-pool-saturation scenario anywhere in the test suite -- called out in both call_timeout_test.exs's own moduledoc SAFETY NOTE and test/specs/REQ-170.md. Did not touch module_registry.ex, capability_gate.ex, or memory_guard.ex. mix format run on every file written/edited (exit 0, no diffs beyond the formatter's own normalization of files I had just written). `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`: clean, 'Compiling 2 files (.ex)' / 'Generated letflow app', zero warnings. Focused run (`mix test test/letflow/engine/wasm/call_timeout_test.exs test/letflow/engine/wasm/plugin_handler_test.exs test/letflow/engine/wasm/resource_limits_test.exs`): 'Finished in 5.7 seconds ... Result: 38 passed', zero failures. Full suite (`mix test`, single clean run after an earlier accidental double-concurrent run produced transient DB-contention failures unrelated to this change, diagnosed and re-run cleanly): 'Finished in 648.4 seconds (10.5s async, 637.9s sync) / Result: 2385 passed (5 properties, 2380 tests), 3 excluded' -- zero failures. `mix letflow.lint_handoffs`: 'letflow.lint_handoffs: OK -- 0 new violations across 1267 handoff files (25 pre-existing grandfathered, traced to ISS-0190).' Committed to feature/WF02-REQ170-20260828; not pushed, merged, or self-approved. Routes next to SECURITY-REVIEWER (tenant-data-path adjacent via the broader WASM containment story) and REVIEWER per the workflow -- I am not marking my own handoff as passing those gates.
